extracted.intended_audience: users of the PARI/GP computer algebra library; computational number theorists and mathematicians programming with PARI/GP
extracted.subtask_description: A section of the PARI/GP library manual documenting functions for quadratic fields, classical number-theory utilities, discrete-log/factor tools, and elliptic-curve functionality; includes calling conventions, parameter constraints, returned types, warnings and performance notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: quadclassunit0 / Buchquad c2 behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: quadclassunit0(Buchquad) uses a bound of norm ≤ c2 (log |D|)^2 to generate class/unit groups; by default an optimal c2 is chosen so the result is provably correct under GRH. Bach shows c2 = 6 suffices; user-supplied smaller c2 values are ignored; larger c2 values increase runtime but not correctness (under GRH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If experimenting with the tech parameter use Buchquad(GEN D, double c1, double c2, long prec). The implementation uses a provably-correct default c2; changing it can lengthen computations. Results are provably correct assuming GRH; Bach's c2=6 is a safe choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: quaddisc
rubrics_metrics.description: quaddisc(x): returns the discriminant of the quadratic field Q(sqrt(x)), where x ∈ Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN quaddisc(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadgen
rubrics_metrics.description: quadgen(D): creates the quadratic number ω = (a + sqrt(D))/2 with a chosen so (1,ω) is an integral basis for the quadratic order of discriminant D. D must be an integer ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 4) and not a square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN quadgen(GEN D). a = 0 if D ≡ 0 mod 4, a = 1 if D ≡ 1 mod 4. Returns a quadratic number suitable as basis element (see Section 3.4.72).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadhilbert
rubrics_metrics.description: quadhilbert(D): returns a relative equation defining the Hilbert class field of the quadratic field of discriminant D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For D < 0 the implementation uses complex multiplication (Schertz's variant). For D > 0 it uses Stark units and may return a vector of extensions whose compositum is the class field; see bnrstark for details. Library syntax: GEN quadhilbert(GEN D, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadpoly
rubrics_metrics.description: quadpoly(D, {v = x}): creates the canonical quadratic polynomial (in variable v) corresponding to discriminant D, i.e. the minimal polynomial of quadgen(D). D must be integer ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 4) and not a square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN quadpoly0(GEN D, long v = -1) where v is a variable number.

rubrics_metrics.name: quadray
rubrics_metrics.description: quadray(D, f): relative equation for the ray class field of conductor f for the quadratic field of discriminant D using analytic methods. A bnf for x^2 − D is also accepted in place of D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For D < 0 uses the σ function and Schertz’s method. For D > 0 uses Stark’s conjecture and may return a vector of relative equations; see bnrstark for details. Library syntax: GEN quadray(GEN D, GEN f, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadregulator
rubrics_metrics.description: quadregulator(x): returns the regulator of the quadratic field of positive discriminant x. Returns an error if x is not a discriminant or if x is a square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x is large, consider using quadclassunit. Library syntax: GEN quadregulator(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadunit
rubrics_metrics.description: quadunit(D): returns the fundamental unit of the real quadratic field Q(sqrt(D)), where D is the positive discriminant of the field. If D is not a fundamental discriminant, the function probably returns the fundamental unit of the corresponding order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D must be an integer ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 4) and not a square. Result is a quadratic number (see quadgen). Library syntax: GEN quadunit(GEN D).

rubrics_metrics.name: randomprime
rubrics_metrics.description: randomprime({N = 2^31}): returns a strong pseudoprime in [2, N−1]. A vector interval [a,b] is allowed and a pseudo-prime a ≤ p ≤ b is returned; if no prime exists the function may loop indefinitely. If the upper bound < 2^64 the returned pseudo-prime is a proven prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN randomprime(GEN N = NULL). Beware infinite loops if interval contains no prime. For small bounds (<2^64) output is guaranteed prime.

rubrics_metrics.name: removeprimes
rubrics_metrics.description: removeprimes({x = []}): removes primes listed in x from the prime number table. If x omitted, lists current extra primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: x can be a single integer. removeprimes(addprimes()) empties the extra prime table. Library syntax: GEN removeprimes(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: sigma / sumdivk
rubrics_metrics.description: sigma(x, {k = 1}) (GEN sumdivk): sum of the k-th powers of the positive divisors of |x|. x and k must be integers. sumdiv(n) is provided for k=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN sumdivk(GEN x, long k). Also GEN sumdiv(GEN n) available.

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrtint
rubrics_metrics.description: sqrtint(x): returns the integer square root of x, i.e. the largest integer y with y^2 ≤ x, for non-negative integer x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows integer and floating comparisons. Library syntax: GEN sqrtint(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrtnint
rubrics_metrics.description: sqrtnint(x, n): returns the integer n-th root of x, i.e. largest integer y such that y^n ≤ x, for non-negative integer x. Special case n=2 equals sqrtint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN sqrtnint(GEN x, long n). Example compares to floating power.

rubrics_metrics.name: stirling / vecstirling
rubrics_metrics.description: stirling(n, k, {flag = 1}): Stirling numbers. flag=1 (default) gives first-kind s(n,k) (signed count of permutations of n symbols with k cycles); flag=2 gives second-kind S(n,k) (number of ways to partition n elements into k non-empty subsets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all s(n,k) or many S(n,k) for same k are needed, there are faster methods using generating products or formulae; simple helper implementations vecstirling and vecstirling2 illustrate efficient variants. Library syntax: GEN stirling(long n, long k, long flag). Also stirling1 and stirling2 available.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumdedekind
rubrics_metrics.description: sumdedekind(h, k): returns the Dedekind sum s(h,k) implemented as sum_{n=1}^{k-1} (n/k) * (frac(h*n/k) - 1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN sumdedekind(GEN h, GEN k).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumdigits
rubrics_metrics.description: sumdigits(n): returns sum of decimal digits of integer n. Other bases than 10 are not supported. For sum of bits use hammingweight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN sumdigits(GEN n). Example: sumdigits(123456789) = 45.

rubrics_metrics.name: zncoppersmith
rubrics_metrics.description: zncoppersmith(P, N, X, {B = N}): Given integer N and polynomial P ∈ Z[X], finds integers x with |x| ≤ X such that gcd(N, P(x)) ≥ B using Coppersmith's algorithm. X must be smaller than exp(log^2 B/(deg(P) log N)); for B=N this implies X < N^{1/deg(P)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller B or larger X slows routine. Strength: finds roots modulo composite N; for prime or prime-power N faster alternatives exist (polrootsmod, polrootspadic). Examples include recovering a factor given partial factor information (fast) and attacks on low-exponent RSA when message is short and padding known. Library syntax: GEN zncoppersmith(GEN P, GEN N, GEN X, GEN B = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: znlog (discrete logarithm)
rubrics_metrics.description: znlog(x, g, {o}): discrete logarithm of x in (Z/NZ)^* base g. Returns [] if x is not a power of g. Optional o denotes multiplicative order of g (preferred format [ord, factor(ord)]) to speed computation. Result undefined if g not invertible mod N or supplied order incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses a combination of generic discrete log routines: Pohlig-Hellman reduction, Shanks baby-step/giant-step for small q, Pollard rho for large q. For prime modulus uses linear-sieve index-calculus for suitable ranges. Complexity notes: Pollard rho and baby-step/giant-step require O(q) ops; Pollard rho can loop if no solution (no detection). g may be p-adic number as convenience. Library syntax: GEN znlog(GEN x, GEN g, GEN o = NULL). Examples and timings given.

rubrics_metrics.name: znorder
rubrics_metrics.description: znorder(x, {o}): returns the multiplicative order of x in (Z/nZ)^*. Returns an error if x not invertible. Optional o represents a non-zero multiple of the order of x; preferred format [ord, factor(ord)] where ord = eulerphi(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN znorder(GEN x, GEN o = NULL). Also available: GEN order(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: znprimroot
rubrics_metrics.description: znprimroot(n): returns a primitive root (generator) of (Z/nZ)^* whenever the group is cyclic (n = 4 or n = 2 p^k or n = p^k with p odd prime and k ≥ 0). If group not cyclic the result is undefined. For prime powers the smallest positive primitive root is returned (except possibly for n = 2 p^k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function requires factoring p−1 for p as above to determine exact order of elements — this can be costly for large p. Library syntax: GEN znprimroot(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: znstar
rubrics_metrics.description: znstar(n): gives structure of multiplicative group (Z/nZ)^* as [φ(n), [d1,...,dk], [generators]], where the di divide previous ones and the product of cyclic groups Z/d[i]Z is isomorphic to (Z/nZ)^*. For n=0 returns [2, [2], [-1]] corresponding to Z^*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show how to extract group order, cycle structure and generators, and use znorder on generators. Library syntax: GEN znstar(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: elliptic curve structure (ellinit) overview
rubrics_metrics.description: ellinit initializes an 'ell' structure representing an elliptic curve given Weierstrass coefficients [a1,a2,a3,a4,a6] (or short form [a4,a6] or Cremona label). The structure contains coefficients, invariants (b2,b4,b6,b8,c4,c6,disc,j) and domain-specific cached data computed on demand; precise layout is undefined and should not be accessed directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expensive data are computed lazily and cached. Use ellinit(x, {D = 1}) with optional domain D indicating Q, finite fields, padics or reals. If curve is singular over domain D ellinit returns []. Use minimal models for speed; many routines assume integral models but accept non-minimal ones (may be slower). Some routines require elldata package (Cremona database).

rubrics_metrics.name: ell structure: common members
rubrics_metrics.description: Ell structures (for all domains) include members a1,a2,a3,a4,a6; b2,b4,b6,b8 (b-invariants); c4,c6 (c-invariants); disc (discriminant); j (j-invariant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members are accessible via E.member notation. Values used by many ell-* routines; disc is required to be non-zero (not necessarily a unit).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellperiods / periods conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For curves over R (including Q), ellperiods computes/caches area (lattice volume), roots (complex roots of RHS g(x)), omega = [ω1, ω2] periods basis with conventions: ω1 positive real period, τ = ω1/ω2 lies in Poincaré half-plane (positive imaginary part) so PSL2 acts naturally; eta = quasi-periods [η1,η2] with ηi = 2 ζ(ωi/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning about orientation: many sources use inverse convention ω2/ω1 with positive imaginary part; PARI's convention uses τ = ω1/ω2 (our ω2 is negative of the inverse-convention ω2). Legendre relation η2 ω1 − η1 ω2 = 2 i π holds. Use ellperiods to recompute to current realprecision.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellinit domain handling (Q, Qp, Fq, R)
rubrics_metrics.description: ellinit accepts optional D specifying domain: D=1 (default) for Q; prime p for Fp; Mod(a,p) for Fp; t_FFELT for Fq; t_PADIC O(p^n) for Qp (recommend input model over Q for p-adics); t_REAL for complex numbers with precision control. If approximate p-adic model provided, it is lifted to Q and computations done on lifted model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If coefficients incompatible with domain an error is raised. If model singular over domain returns []. Many functions will compute domain-specific cached data on demand. Use minimal models when possible for speed. Library syntax: GEN ellinit(GEN x, GEN D = NULL, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellL1
rubrics_metrics.description: ellL1(e, r): returns value at s=1 of r-th derivative of L-function of elliptic curve e, assuming r ≤ order of vanishing; result is wrong if r is strictly larger than order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically used after ellanalyticrank to compute leading term at high accuracy for BSD checks. Example shows adjusting realprecision for high-precision computations. Library syntax: GEN ellL1(GEN e, long r, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: elladd
rubrics_metrics.description: elladd(E, z1, z2): sums two points z1 and z2 on elliptic curve E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN elladd(GEN E, GEN z1, GEN z2). Works on affine points represented as [x,y]; point at infinity is [0].

rubrics_metrics.name: ellak / akell
rubrics_metrics.description: ellak(E, n) (alias akell): computes coefficient a_n of L-function of elliptic curve E/Q (Fourier coefficient of corresponding newform). E must be ell structure over Q by ellinit and given by an integral model; minimal models make it faster but not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If model not minimal at bad primes function is slower for n divisible by bad primes. Library syntax: GEN akell(GEN E, GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellan / anell
rubrics_metrics.description: ellan(E, n) (alias anell): computes vector of first n Fourier coefficients a_k corresponding to elliptic curve E. Curve should be integral model; minimal model improves speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: anellsmall is available to return a t_VECSMALL saving memory. Library syntax: GEN anell(GEN E, long n) or GEN anellsmall(GEN E, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellanalyticrank
rubrics_metrics.description: ellanalyticrank(e, {eps}): returns [r, value] where r is order of vanishing at s=1 of L-function and value is first non-zero derivative value. To detect order, values less than eps are treated as zero; default eps is half the current precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show ranks 0..3. Library syntax: GEN ellanalyticrank(GEN e, GEN eps = NULL, long prec). Use with appropriate precision and eps choice to avoid misclassification.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellap
rubrics_metrics.description: ellap(E, {p}): computes trace of Frobenius t for elliptic curve E (so #E(Fq) = q + 1 − t). If E defined over finite field Fq omit p; if defined over Q p must be given and function computes trace of reduction mod p. Equation need not be minimal at p but minimal is more efficient. Reduction may be singular; returns order of non-singular points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithms: if E/Fq has CM use explicit formula O((log q)^2). Otherwise Shanks-Mestre baby-step/giant-step used (O(q^(1/2))? textual q(p1/4) with O(q^(1/4)) storage); SEA algorithm available if seadata package installed (heuristic ~O((log q)^4)) for large primes. In very small characteristic use Harley's algorithm. Library syntax: GEN ellap(GEN E, GEN p = NULL). Examples show error messages when inconsistent moduli passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellbil / bilhell
rubrics_metrics.description: ellbil(E, z1, z2) (bilhell): computes canonical bilinear Néron-Tate form on points z1,z2: (h(E,z1+z2) − h(E,z1) − h(E,z2))/2. z1 or z2 (but not both) may be vectors or matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN bilhell(GEN E, GEN z1, GEN z2, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellcard
rubrics_metrics.description: ellcard(E, {p}): computes cardinality #E(Fq) of the elliptic curve over finite field or of reduction mod p if E over Q and p provided. Reduction may be singular; returns order of group of non-singular points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ellcard(GEN E, GEN p = NULL). Also available: GEN ell-card(GEN E, GEN p) where p not NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellchangecurve
rubrics_metrics.description: ellchangecurve(E, v): changes coordinates of elliptic curve E using vector v=[u,r,s,t] so new coords relate by x = u^2 x' + r, y = u^3 y' + s u^2 x' + t. v=1 is shorthand for trivial change [1,0,0,0].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E must be an ell structure. Library syntax: GEN ellchangecurve(GEN E, GEN v). Use together with ellchangepoint / ellchangepointinv to map points between models.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellchangepoint / ellchangepointinv
rubrics_metrics.description: ellchangepoint(x, v): changes coordinates of point(s) x using v=[u,r,s,t] consistent with ellchangecurve; ellchangepointinv applies inverse isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show mapping a point and inverting to recover original. Library syntax: GEN ellchangepoint(GEN x, GEN v) and GEN ellchangepointinv(GEN x, GEN ch).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellconvertname
rubrics_metrics.description: ellconvertname(name): converts an elliptic curve name (Cremona notation like '123b1') to triplet [conductor, isogeny_class, index] and can convert triplet back to name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ellconvertname(GEN name). Examples: '123b1' ↔ [123,1,1].

rubrics_metrics.name: elldivpol
rubrics_metrics.description: elldivpol(E, n, {v = x}): returns n-division polynomial f_n for curve E in variable v. Roots of f_n are X-coordinates of E[n]; polynomials defined as per standard formulae (ψ_n etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: explicit small n polynomials f1,f2,f3,f4 given. Library syntax: GEN elldivpol(GEN E, long n, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: elleisnum
rubrics_metrics.description: elleisnum(w, k, {flag = 0}): computes numerical value of Eisenstein series of weight k at lattice w (from ellperiods) using standard q-series; flag non-zero with k=4 or 6 returns elliptic invariants g2 or g3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input w may be [ω1,ω2] or elliptic curve E. Examples and precision considerations included. Library syntax: GEN elleisnum(GEN w, long k, long flag, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: elleta
rubrics_metrics.description: elleta(w): returns quasi-periods [η1, η2] associated to lattice basis w = [ω1, ω2], or for elliptic curve E returns E.eta (quasi-periods associated to E.omega).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN elleta(GEN w, long prec). Example shown for [1,i].

rubrics_metrics.name: ellfromj
rubrics_metrics.description: ellfromj(j): returns coefficients [a1,a2,a3,a4,a6] of a fixed elliptic curve with j-invariant j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ellfromj(GEN j).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellgenerators
rubrics_metrics.description: ellgenerators(E): if E elliptic curve over Q returns Z-basis of free part of Mordell-Weil group (requires elldata database and only available for curves in database); if E over finite field Fq returns minimal set of generators for E(Fq).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires elldata for Q-curves of small conductors. Library syntax: GEN ellgenerators(GEN E).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellglobalred
rubrics_metrics.description: ellglobalred(E): computes arithmetic conductor N, global minimal model coordinate change v, global Tamagawa number c (product of local cp), factorization F of N, and local data vector L where L[i] = elllocalred(E, F[i,1]) with local coordinate change removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E must be an ell structure over Q. Returns [N, v, c, F, L]. Library syntax: GEN ellglobalred(GEN E).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: ellgroup(E, {p}, {flag}): computes structure of group E(Fq) ≅ Z/d1Z × Z/d2Z with d2 | d1. If E defined over Q p must be given to compute reduction mod p; singular reductions return structure of non-singular points. flag=0 returns [d1] or [d1,d2]; flag=1 returns [h, cyc, gen] with h = cardinality, cyc = [d1,d2], gen = [P,Q] (P of order d1; Q may not have exact order d2 without discrete log).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution: Q's order d2 may not be guaranteed without an expensive discrete log. Use ellweilpairing to check orders. Library syntax: GEN ellgroup0(GEN E, GEN p = NULL, long flag) or GEN ellgroup(GEN E, GEN p) (flag=0). Examples and inconsistency warnings shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellheegner
rubrics_metrics.description: ellheegner(E): for elliptic curves over Q assumed of analytic rank 1, returns a non-torsion rational point whose canonical height equals elliptic regulator times analytic Sha (uses Heegner point method).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complexity proportional to sqrt(conductor) times height of point — preferable on strong Weil curves. If curve has even analytic rank the function fails with an error. Library syntax: GEN ellheegner(GEN E).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellheight / ghell (Néron-Tate height)
rubrics_metrics.description: ellheight(E, x, {flag=2}) (ghell alias) computes global Néron-Tate height of point x on elliptic curve E/Q using Cremona's normalization. flag selects algorithm: 0 sigma/theta & Silverman's trick (height is twice Silverman's), 1 Tate's 4n algorithm, 2 Mestre's AGM (quadratic convergence, fastest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E should be ell structure; minimal model speeds computation but is not required. Library syntax: GEN ellheight0(GEN E, GEN x, long flag, long prec) or GEN ghell(GEN E, GEN x, long prec) (flag=2).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellheightmatrix / mathell
rubrics_metrics.description: ellheightmatrix(E, x): given vector x of points returns Gram matrix of Néron-Tate heights (i,j) entry = ellbil(E,x[i],x[j]). Rank of matrix gives rank of set of points; determinant (for a basis) equals regulator (note PARI normalization is twice Cremona's so divide by 2 to match Silverman).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mathell(GEN E, GEN x, long prec). Use to compute regulator and detect linear independence approximately.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellidentify
rubrics_metrics.description: ellidentify(E): looks up elliptic curve E (arbitrary model over Q) in elldata database; returns [[N,M,G], C] where N is Cremona name, M minimal model, G Z-basis of free part of E(Q), and C coordinate change for ellchangecurve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires elldata package. Library syntax: GEN ellidentify(GEN E).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellinit (detailed behavior and errors)
rubrics_metrics.description: ellinit(x, {D = 1}): initialize ell structure; x can be full Weierstrass 5-vector, short [a4,a6], Cremona label, and optional domain D selects computation domain. If coefficients too general only basic operations are supported; if curve singular over D returns []. The result contains minimal set of members and domain-specific dynamic cached data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inconsistencies in modulus/domain occur an error is raised (example with padic moduli mismatch). For curves over Q many routines assume integer coefficients for local computations. Use ellminimalmodel to get minimal model and ellchangepoint / ellchangecurve to map points after changes. Library syntax: GEN ellinit(GEN x, GEN D = NULL, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellisoncurve / oncurve
rubrics_metrics.description: ellisoncurve(E, z): returns 1 if point z is on elliptic curve E, 0 otherwise. If E or z have imprecise coefficients an imprecise equality is attempted. z may be a vector of points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate int oncurve(GEN E, GEN z) does not accept vectors. Library syntax: GEN ellisoncurve(GEN E, GEN z).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellj / jell
rubrics_metrics.description: ellj(x): computes elliptic j-invariant. x must be a complex number with positive imaginary part or convertible into a power series or p-adic number with positive valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN jell(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: elllocalred (local reduction / Kodaira type)
rubrics_metrics.description: elllocalred(E, p): calculates Kodaira type of local fiber of elliptic curve E at prime p. E must be an ell structure with integer coefficients ai. Result is a 4-component vector [f, kod, v, c] where f is exponent of p in arithmetic conductor, kod is Kodaira type code, v and c give further local data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function returns local coordinate change data (which ellglobalred removes/replaces with 0). Kodaira type coding is documented but not fully included here. Library syntax: GEN elllocalred(GEN E, GEN p).
